flags.note: The construct שֶׁלּוֹ for genitive 'of it' may reflect Greek influence. Native Hebrew would more likely use construct state פֶסֶל הַחַיָּה or a simple pronominal suffix.
Use of שֶׁל genitive construction may reflect Greek τοῦ influence. Classical Hebrew would prefer construct state שִׁירַת מֹשֶׁה.
The שֶׁ- relative clause construction is standard in Mishnaic Hebrew, so this is natural for the period and not necessarily Greek influence.
Use of שֶׁל genitive instead of construct state חֲגוֹר זָהָב may reflect Greek influence on genitive expression.
The שֶׁ- relative construction is standard in late Hebrew and not necessarily indicative of Greek influence.
Repeated use of שֶׁל genitive construction rather than construct state קְעָרוֹת זָהָב suggests possible Greek syntactic influence.
The שֶׁ- temporal clause is acceptable in late Hebrew, though עַד + infinitive construct would be more classical.
